qa_pairs.question: How many mercury switches are in the acceleration pick-up for the BMW 325 iX?
qa_pairs.answer: There are two mercury switches, one each for forward and reverse drive, which are installed in longitudinal direction of car at an angle to the horizontal.

qa_pairs.question: What resistance value indicates closed contact in the horizontal position for the mercury switches?
qa_pairs.answer: The series connected mercury switches provide closed contact in horizontal position with resistance less than 1 k-ohm.

qa_pairs.question: What resistance value will cause the contact to open when the car experiences negative acceleration?
qa_pairs.answer: Negative acceleration (braking) of the car or inclination of the acceleration transmitter will displace the mercury filling and cause the contact to open with resistance greater than 2.5 M-ohms.

qa_pairs.question: What percentage of braking deceleration is necessary to open the contact?
qa_pairs.answer: Braking deceleration of 35 to 45% is necessary to open the contact because the glass tube is inclined in such a manner.

qa_pairs.question: How can the braking deceleration value for forward drive be simulated?
qa_pairs.answer: The braking deceleration value for forward drive can be simulated by inclining the acceleration pick-up from 19.5 to 24° (with Special Tool 34 5 150 this is equal to 26.5 to 33.0 mm (1.043 to 1.299")).

qa_pairs.question: Does the switching point for reverse drive require adjustment?
qa_pairs.answer: No, the switching point for reverse drive does not have to be adjusted.

qa_pairs.question: What makes the BMW 325 iX unique in terms of drive system features?
qa_pairs.answer: BMW 325 iX (all wheel drive) is the first standard production car to have permanent all wheel drive with constantly switched central and rear axle locks and also a continuously effective ABS.

qa_pairs.question: What is the primary duty of the acceleration pick-up in the BMW 325 iX?
qa_pairs.answer: The acceleration pick-up performs the duty of providing information on road condition (higher or lower traction) so that all three systems can be effective simultaneously in the BMW 325 iX (all wheel drive).

qa_pairs.question: How does the ABS control unit use the acceleration pick-up information?
qa_pairs.answer: The ABS control unit will decide between various data fields depending on the switch condition (open or closed mercury switches), and consequently consider the traction condition of a street or road.

qa_pairs.question: What happens when an open switch condition is detected for longer than 20 seconds?
qa_pairs.answer: If an open switch condition (resistance greater than 2.5 M-ohms) is reported to the ABS control unit over a period of time longer than 20 seconds, the ABS switches off and reports this to the driver with a warning lamp in the instrument cluster.

qa_pairs.question: What tool is mentioned for simulating the braking deceleration value?
qa_pairs.answer: Special Tool 34 5 150 is mentioned for simulating the braking deceleration value, which corresponds to inclining the acceleration pick-up from 19.5 to 24°.

qa_pairs.question: What systems need to work simultaneously in the BMW 325 iX according to this page?
qa_pairs.answer: All three systems - permanent all wheel drive with constantly switched central and rear axle locks and continuously effective ABS - need to be effective simultaneously, requiring a sensor to provide road condition information.
